---
title: "Validation status"
---

This chapter records what has and has not been run, so nobody has to guess.
It is written by hand after each test round and contains only observed facts.
Nothing here is a benchmark or a biological result.

## Automated tests (no real tools)

`pytest -q tests` runs on any machine with Snakemake 8.27.1, pandas, numpy,
plotly and pytest (no conda, no STAR). It covers:

- Snakemake **dry runs** against tiny placeholder inputs (full, processing-only,
  analysis-only, trimming, per-sample tracks, GSEA branch, bad configs rejected,
  the FASTA/GTF chromosome-name check);
- the Python scripts (gene table, count matrix, scale factors, QC summary, QC
  report) on **synthetic** inputs;
- the pure-logic parts of the R scripts (ranking, classification, design checks);
- that the rule-graph diagrams in the docs are current.

At the last run, 80 tests passed. These tests show the workflow parses and that
the scripts behave on made-up inputs. They do **not** show that STAR, DESeq2 or any
other tool gives good results.

## Real-data test (one round, one cluster)

**What was run.** Four TT-seq samples from the public GEO series GSE260914
(mouse ESC, ZFP143 dTAG degron): DMSO and 2 h, two replicates each. Only the
**first 3 million read pairs** of each run were used (44 nt reads), so these are the
first reads in each file, not a random sample. The reference was the mm10 genome
with GENCODE vM25 annotation. The workflow ran on a SLURM cluster (Case Western's Pioneer, `pioneer` profile) with per-rule conda
environments on linux-64.

**What happened.**

- All 59 jobs completed, after one failure that was fixed: MultiQC 1.14 failed at
  import (`No module named 'pkg_resources'`) because the newest setuptools no longer
  provides it; `envs/ttpipe_multiqc.yml` now pins `setuptools<70`, and only that job
  was re-run.
- A first environment build also failed once because conda's package cache filled the
  user's home-directory quota. This is a site issue, not a pipeline one; set
  `CONDA_PKGS_DIRS` to a roomy location (see [Cluster](cluster.qmd)).
- All six conda environments solved on linux-64, including STAR 2.7.9a with
  samtools 1.12 and Picard 2.25.6 in one environment.
- The QC report's parsers read the real STAR `Log.final.out`, the Picard
  MarkDuplicates metrics, STAR `ReadsPerGene`, and the HTSeq counts without errors.
  The MultiQC page found the FastQC, STAR and Picard reports for all four samples.

**Observed values on this subset** (illustrative of the report, not a quality
statement about the data):

| Quantity | Observed range over 4 samples |
|---|---|
| Uniquely mapped (STAR) | 62.3 to 66.2 % |
| Multi-mapped | 7.7 to 8.4 % |
| Unmapped, too short | 24.2 to 29.2 % |
| Duplication (Picard) | 22.5 to 32.1 % |
| Reads on the gene strand (HTSeq, `sum` counting) | 86.7 to 88.4 % |
| rRNA genes, % of counted reads | 8.5 to 12.9 % |
| Replicate correlation (Pearson, log2 CPM) | 0.943 (DMSO), 0.956 (2 h) |

Against the default thresholds in the config, the strand, rRNA and DMSO replicate
correlation values fall in the **warn** range. The thresholds' `fail` values are
TTpipe defaults, not literature values.

DESeq2 (2 h vs DMSO, alpha 0.01) tested 11,209 genes and called 1 up and 17 down.
With two replicates and a 3-million-pair subset this says nothing about the biology.

**Measured resource use** (from Snakemake benchmark files in this run):
STAR alignment used about 25.7 GB of memory (depends on the genome, not the number
of reads) and the STAR index build about 28.9 GB and 36 minutes. Every other rule
used roughly 1.2 GB or less. Run times are for 3-million-pair inputs only and do not
extrapolate to full-depth samples; the per-rule values in the profiles remain
starting values.

## What has not been run

- **Full-depth data.** The real samples have roughly 30 to 48 million pairs; none were run.
- **Time points 6 h and 24 h**, so the **multi-comparison Sankey** (this subset has one
  contrast, which uses the one-comparison bar chart) and multi-contrast DESeq2 are untested on real data.
- **fgsea / GSEA.** No gene-set files were configured, so the `rnk` and `fgsea` rules did not run.
  The Java GSEA tool was never compared with fgsea.
- **Optional switches** on real data: `trim: true` (fastp), `strandedness: forward`,
  `count_strand: sense`, `sample_tracks: true`, `analysis_counts`.
- **Other clusters and platforms.** Only one cluster was used. STAR 2.7.9a, samtools
  1.12 and HTSeq 0.13.5 have no osx-arm64 builds, so a laptop run on Apple silicon was not attempted.
- **Spike-in, labeled-vs-total and rate analyses** do not exist in this version.

## Repeating the real-data test

1. List the TT-seq runs of GSE260914 with the ENA read-only API (filter
   `study_alias="GSE260914"`; select runs whose title starts with `TTseq_`).
2. Subsample reads, for example with `gunzip -c ... | head -n 12000000 | gzip`
   per mate for 3 million pairs, and check that the line counts and read IDs of mate
   1 and mate 2 match (a dropped connection can truncate a stream).
3. Use a FASTA and GTF with the same chromosome naming, set `build_star_index: true`
   and `sjdb_overhang` to read length minus 1.
4. Build the environments on a node with internet
   (`bash TTpipe.sh --conda-create-envs-only`), then submit `TTpipe.sh`.
